sentences.text: Palaeophasianus was an extinct genus of flightless birds belonging to the family Geranoididae that lived in North America during the Eocene.
The only known species, Palaeophasianus meleagroides, is described as a ground-dwelling carnivore.
Fossil remains of Palaeophasianus were discovered in 1910 by the American Museum expedition in Big Horn County, Wyoming, within the Willwood formation.
Robert Wilson Shufeldt described the genus Palaeophasianus in 1913, initially classifying it as a galliform.
The classification of Palaeophasianus was later revised, with Pierce Brodkorb moving it to Cracidae in 1964 and Joel Cracraft placing it in Gruiformes in 1968.
According to the Paleobiology Database, the parent group of Palaeophasianus is Phasianinae and the family is listed as Phasianidae.
However, the Paleobiology Database incorrectly classifies Palaeophasianus under the class Reptilia.
Palaeophasianus lived during the Ypresian stage of the Eocene, between 56 and 51.1 million years ago.
